what_its_for: Chenodiol is used to dissolve certain types of gallstones (called cholesterol gallstones) in people who cannot have surgery to remove them. It works by reducing the amount of cholesterol your body produces and releases into bile, which helps shrink and slowly dissolve the stones over time.
how_to_take: Take chenodiol by mouth with food or milk to help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level of the medicine in your body. Do not crush or chew the tablets unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 13 to 16 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, split into two doses (morning and evening). Your doctor will calculate the right dose for your specific weight and condition. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose without talking to them first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store chenodiol at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum (such as Maalox or Mylanta) within 2 hours of your chenodiol dose, as they can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed. Avoid cholesterol-lowering medicines called bile acid sequestrants (such as cholestyramine or colestipol) unless your doctor approves, as they can also interfere with absorption. Limit high-cholesterol and high-fat foods to help the medicine work better. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, cramping, or diarrhea that does not go away; yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice); dark urine or very pale stools; unusual tiredness or weakness; nausea or vomiting that is severe; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if you think you might be pregnant.
when_it_works: Chenodiol works slowly. It may take 18 to 24 months of regular treatment before your gallstones are fully dissolved. Your doctor will use ultrasound or X-ray tests every 6 to 12 months to check how well the medicine is working. It is very important to keep taking the medicine every day as prescribed, even if you feel fine. Gallstones can come back after treatment stops.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use chenodiol if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm to the unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and talk to your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if chenodiol passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established. Older adults: Use with caution; your doctor may monitor your liver function more closely. Liver disease: This medicine is not recommended if you have active liver disease or certain bile duct problems. Tell your doctor about all medical conditions before starting treatment.
